title: Lookahead decoding: kernel routing, KV-cache onboarding criteria and rollback playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for integrating "lookahead"-style decoding into the serving runtime. By "lookahead" we mean a hybrid speculative mechanism that probes one or more next-token candidates at low-priority/cheap kernels to inform scheduling, batching and kernel selection without fully committing client-visible tokens until a final selection is made. This doc focuses on three practical areas that must be operationalized for model onboarding: (1) kernel routing rules and heuristics, (2) KV-cache management and scheduling impact, and (3) acceptance/rollback criteria and metrics to gate rollouts.

Context and motivation (short):
- Our runtime already supports multiple kernel backends with differing latency/throughput characteristics (FP16 native, int8-quantized kernels, optimized fused-attention kernels for long context, tiled vs streaming-friendly kernels).
- Lookahead probes allow us to reduce tail latency by pre-warming KV cache and choosing kernels based on candidate branching cost. They also enable more aggressive batching without increasing perceived latency.
- But probes add extra compute and more complex KV cache state. Without tight gating and rollback paths we risk cost regressions and correctness/consistency issues.

Non-goals:
- This doc is not a full spec for a new attention algorithm. It is pragmatic: how to introduce probes into serving with clear onboarding/rollback checks for a new model variant.

Key concepts (quick defs):
- Lookahead probe: lightweight inference for a short prefix or single token that runs on a candidate kernel to estimate cost/latency and prime KV state.
- Probe budget: per-request or per-route limit of extra tokens/time allowed for probes.
- Probe affinity: mapping of probe types to kernels (e.g., single-token softmax probe -> int8-fast kernel; 8-token mini-run -> FP16 kernel to test memory behavior).
- KV-shadow: an ephemeral KV cache state created by probes that may be merged into the main KV cache when the probe outcome is accepted.

Design goals and constraints:
- Preserve determinism for responses when model sampling/seed is controlled (we cannot leak probe side-effects into returned tokens unless explicitly accepted).
- Keep cost overhead bounded: default probe budget <= 5% additional token cost or capped to N microseconds of GPU time per request in low-latency routes.
- Keep rollback simple: if metrics regress beyond a threshold, automatically disable probes and fall back to baseline kernel routing.
- Provide observability: token-level cost attribution, probe hit/miss rates, KV-shadow merge counts, and per-kernel probe latency distributions.

High-level flow (per request) - initial proposal:
1) Request arrives. Route to policy: if route has lookahead enabled (config flag per-route/per-model), attempt probe stage.
2) Probe scheduler decides whether to run a quick probe based on current system load, per-customer budget, and route/coldness heuristics.
3) If selected, spawn probe tasks on low-priority worker or on different kernel (cheap kernel by affinity). Probe returns: candidate token logits, kernel latency, and a small profiling bundle (mem footprint, KV touches).
4) Use probe outputs to: a) pre-warm KV (create KV-shadow), b) select primary kernel for final decode, c) decide whether to accept streaming early results (if we have high confidence).
5) If probe accepted (per-rollout policy), merge KV-shadow into main cache and resume/resume decode on chosen kernel. If probe rejected (e.g., stale, changed prompt, or probe TTL expired) discard KV-shadow and proceed with baseline decode.

Kernel routing heuristics (rules set):
- Kernel affinity table: maintain a table mapping model variant, sequence-length range, and probe profile to preferred kernels. This should be editable via the model manifest.
- Cost-benefit threshold: require that expected saved latency > probe cost * safety_factor. Safety_factor defaults to 1.5 (tunable).
- Cold-start override: for cold KV (no existing cache), allow a slightly higher probe budget to prime multi-token KV-shadow (up to 8 tokens) but only if customer/route configured to allow.
- Load-aware throttling: when node GPU utilization > threshold (80% by default) or pending queue depth > X, automatically rate-limit probes by sampling ratio.
- Fallback mapping: define fallback kernel variants explicitly for each primary kernel to support graceful degradation (e.g., if fused-attn kernel OOMs, fall back to tiled-fp16).

KV-cache semantics and bookkeeping:
- KV-shadow lifecycle: create ephemeral KV-storage per probe with versioned keys tied to request-id and probe-id. Attach TTL (short, e.g., 30s).
- Merge semantics: merges must be atomic from the perspective of the request: either the shadow becomes the new active KV state reachable by the continuation decode or it is dropped. For multi-request caching (shared prefixes across requests) we only promote KV-shadow to shared cache if policy allows optimistic sharing and probe was run in a trusted mode.
- Consistency checks: before merging, validate that the live main KV cache still corresponds to the same prompt hash and hasn't been mutated by other concurrent continuations. If mismatch, abort merge.
- Memory accounting: track ephemeral KV bytes separately in the node accounting so autoscaler can account for probe inflation spikes. If ephemeral+resident KV exceeds node limit, refuse new probes.

Acceptance criteria for onboarding a model variant with lookahead enabled:
(These are minimum gating checks for product rollout to beta/GA.)
A) Functional correctness checks (automated):
  - Deterministic baseline parity: for a fixed deterministic sampling configuration (seeded), responses with probes disabled must match baseline serving outputs. With probes enabled, final committed tokens must match baseline when model/weights unchanged (except for allowed non-determinism by sampling policies).
  - No token corruption: ensure merging KV-shadow never produces tokenization/hypothesis divergence (unit tests covering edge token boundaries, multi-byte tokens).
B) Performance checks (metrics over a 48h canary):
  - Latency P50, P95, P99 must not regress more than X% over baseline (defaults: P50 < +5%, P95 < +10%, P99 < +20%).
  - Cost per 1k tokens (GPU-time) increase must be <= 5% for GA routes (<= 10% for experimental routes).
  - Tail latency improvements: at least one of P95 or P99 shows measurable decrease vs baseline in real workload (if not, probe not useful).
C) Stability and error rate:
  - Error rates (OOMs, 5xx infra errors) must not increase more than 0.1 percentage points over baseline.
  - KV-merge abort rate should be tracked — target < 0.5% merges aborted due to stale state under normal traffic.
D) Observability/telemetry coverage:
  - Probe events must include token-level attribution, kernel id, probe latency, KV-shadow size, merge result. All must be present in telemetry payloads for at least 100% of requests in canary.
  - Traces for end-to-end request when probe runs must be capturable via existing tracing (sampling = 100% for canary).

Rollback gates and automated rollback behavior:
- Fast fail toggle: rollout must attach to an SRE-managed feature-flag with immediate global toggle (kill-switch).
- Automatic rollback triggers (examples):
  - sustained latency/regressions above thresholds for 15 minutes with >= 5% traffic impact -> auto-disable probes for that model/route.
  - OOMs > 0.05% in a node pool in 10m window -> start draining that node's probe tasks and rollback on pool.
  - Merge-abort spike: if merge-abort rate > 2% in 1h -> pause lookahead and notify oncall.
- Soft rollback: instead of fully disabling probes, step down probe sampling rate (50% -> 25% -> 0) and auto-observe for regressions. This staged rollback reduces blast radius and provides data about marginal cost/benefit.

Metrics to collect (explicit list for instrumentation):
- probe_attempts_total (by route, model_variant, kernel)
- probe_success_total (probe completed without internal error)
- probe_latency_ms{quantiles}
- probe_cost_gpu_ms (approx GPU-time consumed)
- kv_shadow_bytes_allocated_total
- kv_shadow_merge_count, kv_shadow_merge_abort_count (and abort_reasons tag)
- kernel_selection_changes_due_to_probe_total
- per-token_cost_delta (delta between baseline token cost and with-probe token cost)
- end_to_end_latency_{p50,p95,p99}
- error_5xx_rate, oom_rate, kernel_fallback_rate

Canary rollout plan (practical):
1) Unit/integration tests + local perf harness (simulate probe budget saturated).
2) Internal dogfood: enable on internal team routes for 24–48h with high telemetry sampling.
3) Stage canary: 1% of traffic on a non-critical region/route for 4h (monitor probes metrics at 1m resolution). If no issues, 5% for 12h.
4) Progressive ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 12h at each stage and SLOs checked. Use soft rollback steps on anomalies.

Runbook (oncall steps) - quick reference:
- Alert: probe_error_rate_high or probe_cost_spike -> first check rolling median probe_latency and GPU utilization. If utilization > 90%, disable probes for this pool and notify infra.
- Alert: kv_merge_abort_spike -> check prompt-hash mismatch counts; if > threshold, disable optimistic KV-share and escalate to engineering.
- Alert: kernel_oom_event -> mark kernel unhealthy, force-fallback mapping and rollback lookahead for models using that kernel.
- Emergency: feature-flag kill-switch always accepted by pager duty rotation owner.

Open questions / TODOs (practical):
- Should we allow optimistic KV sharing across requests for multi-tenant caches? Security/PII concerns need review (CC: security).
- What is the safe default probe budget across different SLAs (free-tier vs enterprise)? Should be in pricing model doc. (Action: product to define tiers).
- How to encode probe affinity in manifest so model teams can express custom probe kernels? Need schema change proposal.
- We need a small simulated load generator that can replay probe-specific load to stress ephemeral KV accounting. Engineering task: ENG-1437.
- Benchmark: design microbench that measures effective saved tokens-per-probe and break-even point per kernel pair.

Appendix: quick checklist for onboarding review (to be used by Solutions/SE):
- [ ] Model manifest includes probe_allowed: true/false and probe_affinity recommended kernel id.
- [ ] Baseline performance profile (p50/p95/p99) captured for identical traffic profile.
- [ ] Canary plan attached with rollback criteria and kill-switch owner.
- [ ] Telemetry panel created (probe attempts, merges, latency, cost) and alert thresholds set.
- [ ] Security reviewed: KV-shadow never writes customer PII to shared persistent caches unless explicitly approved.
- [ ] Cost approval: finance sign-off if projected > 5% cost uplift for target workload.

Notes to self / rough ideas: (shorthand, will refine)
- Consider using a small LRU for ephemeral KV to avoid big spikes when many probes run concurrently.
- For multi-token probes, use truncated attention so we can run on streaming-optimized kernels that don't need full context.
- Investigate option of offloading probe logits scoring to CPU to reduce GPU churn for tiny probes (but watch latency).

References and links:
- Related design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SPEC-DECODE-INTG (internal)
- Kernel catalog: internal doc with kernel performance profiles (ask infra for latest CSV)
- ENG ticket: ENG-1289 (lookahead scheduling prototype)

End.
